newsitem.title: CANADA: Gulf, Talisman well expands Indonesia find.
newsitem.headline: Gulf, Talisman well expands Indonesia find.

text.p: Gulf Canada Resources Ltd and Talisman Energy Inc said Tuesday they drilled a successful step-out well that indicated a much bigger natural accumulation than was expected following their 1995 Sumpal-1 discovery well in Indonesia.
"This has the potential to be a major discovery, which is always a treat with step-out wells," said Gulf Canada spokesman John Sparks.
The step-out, Sumpal-2, is located 3.0 km from the original discovery well on the Corridor Block Production Sharing Contract area in Indonesia.
The companies said it flowed at a maximum rate of 10.2 million cubic feet of raw gas per day through a one-inch choke from a zone at a depth of 2,531 to 2,566 metres.

Gulf and Talisman, partners in the Corridor project, said the test proved hydrocarbons were present 665 metres deeper than previously tested on the geological structure and indicated a gas column of at least 750 metres.
The companies said they planned to test higher potential intervals in Sumpal-2 to gain more information on gas reservoir characteristics.
An analysis of the carbon dioxide content would then be done.
Sumpal-1 flowed at about 35 million cubic feet of gas per day from a pay zone 100 metres thick. The gas had a CO2 content of 34 percent.
The most recent test was about 500 metres deeper than the total depth of Sumpal-1, Sparks said.
"We assume as we move uphole (on the step-out well) we're going to hit some zones that are much more prospective than this one, zones we were actually going for," he said.
Testing and analysis at Sumpal-2 are expected to be completed by late November, the companies said.

Gulf unit Asamera (Overseas) Ltd, is operator and has a 54 percent interest in the Corridor Block PSC. Talisman subsidiary Talisman (Corridor) Ltd has a 36 percent interest Indonesian state oil company Pertamina has 10 percent. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
